queries: The distributed traffic signal system operates through an emergent consensus mechanism where intersections negotiate timing parameters through iterative message passing to achieve system-wide coherence Each intersection maintains multiple candidate timing parameters and evaluates them based on local metrics. It then shares these candidates with neighbors, which in turn evaluate them based on their local context. Through iterative rounds of evaluation and sharing, the system converges to a consensus set of parameters that represents a balance between local efficiency and global coherence. This mimics the consensus-building behavior observed in slime mold network formation.
sources: The Lotus Effect: Superhydrophobicity and Self-Cleaning
